column4: In the previous two chapters we have discussed several important topics. We explored the role and ministry of the Holy Spirit, as well as the role and ministry of the church.

column4: We have a part to play in the church, and while we know that we need training, we also need purification. To really be prepared for God’s purposes we must be sanctified.
column5: We each have a part in the Church; we know training is needed, and cleansing is needed. To be truly prepared for God's purposes, we must be sanctified.

column4: The definition of **sanctification** is to purify something for a special purpose. This is closely related to the term **consecration** which means to set something aside for a special purpose.
column5: The definition of **sanctification** is to make something clean for a special purpose. This is closely related to the term **consecration**, which means to set something apart exclusively for special use.

column4: Imagine a master sculptor preparing to work with a large block of marble. The master imagines what this raw and unshaped marble can be transformed into through his careful craftsmanship. He has a very specific design in mind, he orders his assistants to set this block of marble aside for a special design (**consecration**). As he refines and works the marble, adding texture, depth, and shape, he purifies it (**sanctifies**) for that special design. The act of dedicating the marble for his special project was quick, whereas the process of shaping the marble into its final design takes considerable patience.
column5: Imagine a master sculptor preparing to carve a large block of marble. The master envisions what this raw, unshaped marble can be transformed into through his meticulous craftsmanship. He has a very specific design in mind and instructs his assistant to set this marble apart for that special design (**consecration**). As he refines and polishes the marble, adding texture, depth, and shape, he makes it clean for that special design (**sanctification**). The act of dedicating the marble to his special project is quick, but sculpting it into the final design takes considerable patience.

column4: We were set aside, consecrated to God at salvation. Through the act of purifying our souls by the help of the Spirit we become transformed. This process of purification is what sanctifies us.
column5: When we are saved, we are set apart, set apart unto God. Through the help of the Holy Spirit to cleanse our soul, we are transformed. This cleansing process is what sanctifies us.

column4: When we received Jesus through salvation, we were born-again. We were justified, our sins forgiven. Our spirit was regenerated, we became alive in Christ. We were adopted into the family of God and became the literal temple of the Holy Spirit. Such a marvelous transformation that the scriptures say, “*there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.” (*Luke 15:10).
column5: When we receive Jesus through salvation, we are born again. We are justified, and our sins are forgiven. Our spirit is renewed and made alive in Christ. We are adopted into God's family, becoming a true temple of the Holy Spirit. Of such a marvelous transformation, the Scripture says: “*There is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents.*” (*Luke 15:10).

column4: Receiving Jesus by salvation (**justification**) saves our spirit, cleanses us, and makes us presentable to God, able to receive His Holy Spirit. However, despite such a great salvation **our souls** (our mind, will, and emotions) still **need work**!
column5: Receiving Jesus through salvation (**justification**) saves our spirit and cleanses us, enabling us to stand before God and receive His Holy Spirit. However, despite such a great salvation, **our soul** (our mind, will, and emotions) still **needs work**!

column4: Was the work of salvation incomplete? No! The work of salvation is effective but must be continued in the life of the believer by the renewal brought on by the Holy Spirit. This process of renewal and transformation is the work of **sanctification.**
column5: Is the work of salvation incomplete? No! The work of salvation is effective, but it must continue to be applied in the life of the believer through the renewal brought by the Holy Spirit. This process of renewal and transformation is the work of **sanctification**.

column4: The word ‘carnal’ comes from the Latin root meaning ‘flesh’ or ‘meat.’ The carnal nature is inside of each of us from birth, like an animal’s instincts, it exists to help us survive. The way the carnal nature works is by being self-focused, self-oriented, self-centered. Children are natural examples of a fleshly nature. Despite their innocence, their nature is focused primarily on their wants, desires, needs; and ‘watch out!’ if you don’t meet its every expectation.

column4: Pruning is incredibly healthy for a plant. Thinking back to our chapter on repentance, we are called to turn away from dead works (those works that are no longer bearing fruit) and turn toward God. The result of this turning away from the dead places in our life, and towards God, empowers the great gardener of our life to prune branches, improve growth, and produce greater spiritual fruit (John 15:2).
column5: Pruning is very beneficial for plants. Recall our chapter on repentance: we are called to turn from dead works (acts that no longer bear fruit) and turn to God. This turning away from the dead places in our lives and turning to God allows the great Gardener of our lives to prune the branches, improve growth, and bear more spiritual fruit (John 15:2).

column4: While pruning can feel painful, it reflects God’s loving care as He shapes us into vessels for His purpose (Hebrews 12:11). Some may feel a sense of loss, even fear, when undergoing the pruning process. However, God is gentle, and even a bruised reed He will not break (Isaiah 42:3). Grapevines are pruned during their dormant season to minimize stress on the plant. The gardener tending the growth will cut back old and woody growth that no longer produces fruit like it used to, this allows the vine to direct energy into the branches with the most potential for good fruit.
column5: Though pruning may feel painful, it reflects God’s loving care as He shapes us into vessels fit for His use (Hebrews 12:11). Some may feel a sense of loss, or even fear, during seasons of pruning. However, God is gentle; a bruised reed He will not break (Isaiah 42:3). Vines are pruned during the dormant season to minimize stress on the plant. A gardener who tends growth cuts away parts that have hardened into wood and no longer bear fruit as they once did, enabling the vine to direct its energy toward the shoots most likely to produce good fruit.

column4: Like a gardener trimming branches to direct growth, God may allow seasons of correction and discipline to refine our faith and character, but His work is patient and kind. God prunes those who abide in him. Our focus is to be more on the abiding in Christ, and less on the work of the pruning.
column5: Just as a gardener guides growth by pruning branches, God may allow seasons of correction and discipline to refine our faith and character, yet His work is patient and loving. God prunes those who abide in Him. Our focus should be more on abiding in Christ and less on the pruning itself.

column4: #### **1. Explicit Memory (Declarative Memory)**
column5: #### **1. Explicit Memory (Declarative Memory)**

column4: **Purpose:** Stores facts, events, and experiences that we can consciously recall. It’s split into two types-**semantic** and **episodic** memory.
column5: **Purpose：** Stores facts, events, and experiences we can consciously recall. It is divided into two types-**semantic** and **episodic** memory.

column4: **Semantic Memory - Facts and Knowledge.** Semantic memory is where we store facts, definitions, and general knowledge-things like historical dates, Bible verses, and practical information. It helps us predict outcomes, make decisions, and avoid danger (e.g., recognizing poisonous plants). While it gives us stability and order, it can also lead to rigidity-an over-reliance on rules rather than adapting to unexpected situations.

column4: **Episodic Memory - Personal Experiences.** Episodic memory stores our personal experiences, tying them to specific times and places-like a wedding day or a traumatic event. These memories provide context, helping us learn from the past and build relationships. However, episodic memory is prone to emotional bias and distortion. Past trauma can create fearful associations, making it difficult to move forward.

column4: Renewing the mind isn’t a quick fix-it’s a process of gradual transformation that is lifelong. Each memory system plays a role in shaping how we think, feel, and act. By intentionally working with the Holy Spirit, applying Scripture, and developing godly habits, we can train our minds to align with God’s truth. Whether addressing past wounds, learning new habits, or staying focused in the moment, God has provided both **spiritual tools** and **practical wisdom** to help us walk in renewal and freedom (2 Corinthians 10:5).
column5: Renewing the mind is not a quick fix——it is a lifelong, gradual process of transformation。Each memory system plays a role in shaping our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors。By consciously partnering with the Holy Spirit, applying Scripture, and cultivating godly habits, we can train our minds to align with God’s truth。Whether addressing past wounds, learning new habits, or staying focused in the present，God has given us **spiritual tools** and **practical wisdom** to help us walk in renewal and freedom（2 Corinthians 10:5）。

column4: Our world is full of trouble, tribulation, and trial. Through the disciplined renewing of the mind, our souls become transformed, and we can live a life of freedom unto God full of the fruit of His Spirit (Galatians 5:22-25).
column5: Our world is filled with hardship, affliction, and trials。Through disciplined mind renewal, our inner life is transformed, and we can live a Godward, free life full of the fruit of His Spirit（Galatians 5:22-25）。
